observation_summary: The compiler failed to resolve typedefs correctly when they were defined within a goog.scope, leading to 'Unknown type' errors. The compiler was incorrectly performing a simple string replacement for aliased types instead of properly expanding the qualified name.
reasoning_summary: The fix involved changing the logic within the `AliasedTypeNode` class. Instead of pre-calculating the expanded string during the traversal (which was insufficient for nested or complex resolutions), the fix updated the class to store the `aliasDefinition` node and perform the expansion dynamically during `applyAlias()`. This is a change to the computational procedure (the algorithm for resolving aliases), not a simple assignment or a missing guard.
evidence_used: The fix modifies the `AliasedTypeNode` class to store `aliasDefinition` instead of a pre-computed string.
The `applyAlias` method was rewritten to perform a more robust string replacement using `aliasDefinition.getQualifiedName()`.
The call site in `ScopedAliases` was updated to pass the `aliasedNode` instead of a pre-computed string.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not just changing a value or initialization; it is changing the logic of how the alias is expanded and applied.
The fix is internal to the `ScopedAliases` class and does not change the interface or contract between components.
